paper.title: Time-Varying Gaussian Process Bandits with Unknown Prior

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying GP bandits with unknown prior (general kernels via MIG)
unmapped: The function f(x,t) is a sample from a spatio-temporal GP prior (time variation governed by the prior, e.g. a time-varying kernel with forgetting rate), not a variation-budget model
The true prior is unknown: the learner knows only a finite set U of candidate GP priors (mean and kernel) containing the true prior
In the continuous case the learner knows the derivative-tail constants a^p, b^p of each candidate kernel and the domain scale r
settings.definition_quote: We consider a problem setting where we wish to maximise an unknown, black-box and spatio-temporal function $f: \mathcal{X} \times [T]  \to \mathbb{R}$ over some compact set $\mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$. ... We also assume the available domain at each time step $\mathcal{X}_t \subseteq \mathcal{X}$ can change in an arbitrary manner, possibly chosen by an adversary. ... We assume that the black-box function and its evolution through time are governed by some prior, i.e., $f \sim p^\star(f)$ ... We also assume we are given access to a set of priors $\mathcal{U}$ ... that contains the true prior

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying GP bandits with unknown prior, squared exponential kernels
unmapped: Spatio-temporal GP prior with time-varying (forgetting rate varepsilon) kernel; function evolves according to the prior
The learner knows only a finite set U of candidate priors containing the true prior
settings.definition_quote: Let all candidate priors utilise the squared exponential kernel

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying GP bandits with unknown prior, Matern kernels
unmapped: Spatio-temporal GP prior with time-varying (forgetting rate varepsilon) kernel; function evolves according to the prior
The learner knows only a finite set U of candidate priors containing the true prior
settings.definition_quote: Let all candidate priors utilise the $\nu$-Matern kernel

symbols.B_tstar: beta_t^{p*} + max_{t'<=t*} sup_x |mu^{p*}(x,t')| + 1, with t* the last iteration where a prior was rejected
symbols.beta_T: max over priors of the confidence parameter beta_T^p
symbols.gamma_T: max over candidate priors of the maximum information gain gamma_T^p

conditions: f ~ p*(f) with p* in U
k^p <= 1 and bounded prior means for every p in U
either |X| finite, or X subset [0,r]^d compact convex with Assumption 3.2 (derivative tail condition) for each prior
tuning: beta_t^p = sqrt(2 log(2|X| pi^2 t^2/delta)) (finite X) or the Assumption-3.2-based expression (infinite X)

source.label: theorem:noregret
source.quote: Let $f \sim p^*(f)$, $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R^2)$ for each $t$ and  $p^* \in \mathcal{U}$ ... Then, Algorithm \ref{alg:unknown_prior_bo_noisy} with probability at least $1 - \delta$ achieves the cumulative regret of at most: R_T \le  \mathcal{O} ( |\mathcal{U}|B_{t^\star} + \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|\xi_T T} +  \beta_T \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|T \gamma}_{T} )

results.notes: Probability over the prior draw of f and noise. Proof gives explicit 2|U|B_{t*} + 2 sqrt(xi_T|U|T) + 2 beta_T sqrt(C T |U| gamma_T). Parameters do not depend on T (paper notes this), so anytime. B_{t*} is random (t* random). Environment mapped as nonstationary_drifting for lack of better vocabulary; time variation comes from a spatio-temporal GP prior.

symbols.eps_tv: forgetting rate varepsilon of the time-varying kernel

conditions: all candidate priors use the squared exponential (time-varying) kernel

source.label: corollary:win
source.quote: Let all candidate priors utilise the squared exponential kernel, we then have that  regret of PE-GP-UCB: $R_T = \Tilde{\mathcal{O}}( |\mathcal{U}| B_{t^\star} + \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|}\max\{T\varepsilon^{1/6}, \sqrt{T}\})$

results.notes: Uses gamma_T = O~(max{T eps^{1/3}, 1}) from Bogunovic et al. 2016.

bound.expression: N_U*B_tstar + sqrt(N_U)*Max(T*eps_tv**((1 - c_mat)/(2*(3 - c_mat))), sqrt(T**(1 + c_mat)))

symbols.eps_tv: forgetting rate varepsilon of the time-varying kernel

conditions: all candidate priors use the nu-Matern (time-varying) kernel

source.label: corollary:win
source.quote: Let all candidate priors utilise the $\nu$-Matern kernel, we then have that regret of PE-GP-UCB: $R_T = \Tilde{\mathcal{O}}(|\mathcal{U}| B_{t^\star} + \sqrt{|\mathcal{U}|}\max\{T\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2} \frac{1 - c}{3 - c}}, \sqrt{T^{1+c}}\})$

results.notes: c defined in the appendix proof as d(d+1)/(2nu + d(d+1)).
